articles.title: Tom Brady's NFL Power Rankings: Which QBs Other Than Josh Allen Have Impressed The GOAT?
articles.summary: Josh Allen is playing "very dangerous football," according to Tom Brady. But is that enough for the Bills to unseat the Seahawks in the GOAT's top 10?
articles.body: Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season didn't feature as much scoring as Week 1, but there were still several quarterbacks who impressed, at least in Tom Brady's eyes. In the most recent edition of Tom Brady's power rankings, the GOAT pinpointed a handful of quarterbacks who have starred through the first two weeks. Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen was among them, with Brady saying that he's playing "very dangerous football" following his five-touchdown performance. But was Allen's performance enough to help the Bills unseat the Seattle Seahawks at No. 1 in his power rankings? Here's a closer look at Brady's top 10. 10. Detroit LionsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: 9 ↓ Brady’s thoughts: I know they sneak in at 1-1, but look, it was a short week in Buffalo. That’s pretty tough. Buffalo was opening up a new stadium. That’s as hard as it gets. Bills Mafia was out in full force. Jared Goff, give him his love. He’s playing lights out. He’s got six touchdowns and no picks in his first two games. I kind of like their prospects here as the season goes on. 9. Las Vegas RaidersRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: Unranked Brady's thoughts: Listen, it’s not hometown bias by me. Their plus-26 point differential is third in the league. Kirk Cousins has six touchdowns in two games. C’mon, that’s pretty impressive. They go on the road and beat the Chargers. Look, undefeated is undefeated. What’s that saying? Just win, baby. 8. Minnesota VikingsRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: Unranked Brady's thoughts: They’re 2-0 in the division with their backup quarterback. What? No Kyler Murray. No J.J. McCarthy. Give Kevin O’Connell and Brian Flores a lot of credit. It’s a great coaching job. They held Chicago to three points. Yeah, the weather was a little nasty. But three points for Chicago a week after the Bears put up 59? Interesting. I think Kevin has amazing IQ, EQ and charisma. I think if you stack all three together, and he’s a great leader of men. So, he’s given his team a scheme advantage, getting them hyped up and ready to play every single game and he’s got an amazing intelligence about what he does. He knows how to read his guys and what they need to hear. He’s always going to put those guys in a position to win. 7. Los Angeles RamsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: Unranked Brady's thoughts: The Australia trip — that’s in the past. That’s way behind them. It’s been overtalked about, overplayed — all of it. They took care of business back at home. Look, they had no Myles Garret, no Puka Nacua and they limited Aaron Donald [against the New York Giants]. This team is more than big names. Davante Adams went off for 195 yards and two tuddies. That’s exactly what they needed to get back on track. 6. Cincinnati BengalsRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 10 ↑ Brady's thoughts: I’m very impressed with this start as well from Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals. A lot of complementary football — that’s what I’m seeing from Cincy. How about that defense? That’s music to the Bengals fans' ears. We haven’t talked about that in a few years. They have eight sacks and four takeaways just to start the season in these first two weeks. That’s winning football. Two catches in Week 1 for Ja’Marr [Chase], but two touchdowns in Week 2 — possibly the catch of the year with that toe-tap on the sideline. 5. Philadelphia EaglesRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 6 ↑ Brady's thoughts: Week 1 was kind of funny and some teams are winning big, but the Eagles are winning close ones. That’s nothing new to Eagles fans. It’s not a bad thing to have a close road test under your belt in September in very hot, humid conditions. They showed a lot of toughness, and that’s not easy to do for a team from the Northeast. 4. Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 7 ↑ Brady's thoughts: Through two games, these four teams have kind of set themselves apart. [Patrick] Mahomes’ rust is completely non-existent. He looked invincible the other night. A vintage overtime performance at Arrowhead with almost 400 yards passing and Travis Kelce going off. Kenneth Walker, he’s been an absolute menace for these defenses. However, I will say their defense needs to find a way to pressure the QB. I’ve got an idea, though: Steve Spagnuolo, that guy calling the plays on defense, he’s the right guy to figure it out. 3. Buffalo BillsRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 5 ↑ Brady's thoughts: The Bills got out to a fast start in their new stadium, which I’m really looking forward to seeing. And Detroit, they were literally playing catch-up the entire night. Tough to go on the road against a team like that; that’s really hot. The Bills’ offense had 36 points against Houston and 41 against Dan Campbell and the Lions. No turnovers across the board from Josh Allen in two games. Very impressive. I’m very impressed with Josh’s ability to eliminate the negative plays. I think early in his career, he was always trying to make a big play. He was a little bit inaccurate in the passing game. He’s really settled down and become an accurate passer. He knows when to take his chances. He’s playing very dangerous football. That’s going to be a tough team to beat. 2. San Francisco 49ersRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 3 ↑ Brady's thoughts: They get home from Australia and that travel didn’t bother them. They dominated the Dolphins. They have a plus-42 point differential this year. That’s almost double the next best in the NFL. Their offense is averaging eight [yards] per play and had no turnovers on Sunday. Are you seeing a trend here? Brock Purdy, how about this guy? He’s just always making the right decisions with his pre-snap reads. I always feel like he’s in total control. He’s very poised. I like the way Purdy’s playing. This Niners team — watch out. No one thought about them. 1. Seattle SeahawksRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 1 Brady's thoughts: In order to be the best, you’ve got to beat the best. Seattle is 2-0, winning in all three phases of the game: offense, defense and special teams. Great complementary football. And who can forget about JSN (Jaxon Smith-Njigba)? He’s got four tuddies in two games. Sam Darnold goes out a few plays into the season and in comes Drew Lock, who is completing 73% of his passes. And even more impressive, I talk about negative plays a lot, he’s had zero interceptions. That’s hard to do. They had 162 yards last week — a true running back by committee. They might miss Kenneth Walker a little bit, but you can’t keep everybody. They seem to have picked the right guys so far. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Yankees Slugger Giancarlo Stanton Could Return For Playoffs After 5-Month Absence
articles.summary: Yankees slugger Giancarlo Stanton could return for the playoffs after a 5 1/2-month absence due to calf strains.
articles.body: Yankees slugger Giancarlo Stanton could return for the playoffs after a 5 1/2-month absence due to calf strains. Stanton faced pitchers Wednesday at Double-A Somerset along with center fielder Trent Grisham, sidelined since straining his right hamstring on Sept. 4. Both ran the bases and Stanton homered while taking six or seven at-bats. "Putting them on the outskirts of the conversation," New York manager Aaron Boone, bothered by a cold, said in a raspy voice. Already without injured star Aaron Judge due to a strained right calf, New York is likely to host Boston in a best-of-three Wild Card Series starting Tuesday, with all three games at Yankee Stadium. Following the end of the seasons for Yankees farm teams, New York has minor leaguers working out at Somerset in nearby New Jersey. Stanton hasn't played since April 24 because of strained calf muscles in both legs after starting the season with a .256 batting average, three homers and 14 RBIs in 24 games. The 36-year-old former NL MVP had 38 homers and 100 RBIs in his first season with New York in 2018 but has missed 500 of 1,194 games since (41.9%), through the end of this regular season. His other injuries included strains of his right biceps, right knee, left hamstring (three times), left quadriceps and both calf muscles along with right ankle inflammation, left Achilles tendinitis and tendon pain in both elbows. "You’re looking more at a pinch-hit scenario," Boone said. "We’ll see if that’s even a realistic option." Stanton is owed $25 million next year in the final guaranteed season of a $325 million, 13-year contract that includes a $10 million buyout of a 2028 club option. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: NFL Catchup: Giants Keeping QB Options Open; Bears Still Unsure On Week 3 Starter
articles.summary: Here's the latest from around the NFL on Wednesday.
articles.body: Wednesday brought some clarity at quarterback in one building and plenty of uncertainty in others, as teams across the league finalized their injury reports ahead of Week 3. The Atlanta Falcons got good news heading into their Thursday night matchup against the Green Bay Packers, while two other franchises are still sorting out who'll actually take the snaps this weekend. Tua Tagovailoa is cleared to back up Michael Penix Jr. on Thursday, but the New York Giants are exploring every option at quarterback after losing Jaxson Dart for the season, and the Chicago Bears still don't know whether Case Keenum, Tyson Bagent or Caleb Williams will start Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles. Here's the latest from around the NFL on Wednesday. Giants Keeping Options Open At QB After Losing Jaxson Dart With Jaxson Dart out for the season, John Harbaugh made clear the Giants aren't ruling anything out at quarterback — including a trade for a starter. Jameis Winston will run the offense in Week 3 against the Titans, but Harbaugh confirmed the team plans to add another arm to the room, even if he wouldn't name candidates. Winston brings experience but hasn't held a full-time starting job since 2019, and Jake Haener is the only other quarterback New York controls, sitting on the practice squad. Tests showed Dart avoided ACL damage, but tears to his MCL, PCL and meniscus will require surgery, with the meniscus the biggest concern — an injury similar to the one that cost Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy his entire 2024 season. McCarthy, now buried on Minnesota's depth chart behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, has reportedly drawn interest as a trade value given Giants GM Joe Schoen's familiarity with him from the 2024 draft process. Harbaugh didn't close the door on Dart returning for a potential postseason run. Case Keenum Practices For Bears Chicago's quarterback picture remains murky ahead of Monday night's game against Philadelphia, with Case Keenum, Tyson Bagent and Caleb Williams all in play depending on health. Keenum, 38, practiced Wednesday and hasn't played in a regular-season game since December 2023, but he's healthy — which is more than can currently be said for the other two. He said he is nervous about possibly starting, but he welcomes the emotions. "I love the feeling of being nervous. I do get nervous. And it's not a scared nervous, it's an excited nervous, because I know I'm prepared. I'm confident in my preparation and what I've done. I'm confident in my teammates. I'm confident in their preparation. I'm confident in the game plan and what my coaches have put together." Williams is still working back from the hamstring injury that knocked him out of Sunday's loss to Minnesota, and while he hasn't been ruled out, caution is expected given how much his mobility factors into his game. Bagent, who went 5 of 9 for 54 yards in relief before getting sacked on the final play, was unexpectedly placed in concussion protocol Tuesday with no clear return timeline. Coach Ben Johnson said the team has no plans to bring in another quarterback this week, framing the uncertainty as an opportunity for whoever ends up under center. Tua Tagovailoa Available For Falcons Thursday Night Tua Tagovailoa is good to go for Atlanta's trip to Green Bay, and he'll be doing so as the backup. The quarterback was not on the Falcons' final injury report of the week, and head coach Kevin Stefanski indicated earlier Wednesday that Tagovailoa was trending toward serving behind Michael Penix Jr. for Thursday Night Football. Tagovailoa was actually slated to start the season opener before an oblique injury suffered during practice week sidelined him, with Cooper Rush filling in for the first two games while Penix worked back from reconstructive knee surgery. Now healthy, Tagovailoa slots in as QB2 behind Penix, who's set to handle starting duties in Week 3. Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks Headed To IR For Surgery Carolina is placing running back Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve after he's set to undergo surgery Wednesday for a core muscle injury, though he's expected to return later this season. The Panthers said Brooks is looking at a minimum six-week recovery after injuring his groin late in Sunday's win over Atlanta. "It was a pretty significant groin injury, and we got multiple opinions about what's the best course of action," head coach Dave Canales said. "Jonathon's gonna have surgery to repair the injury, and the timeline of return with surgical or nonsurgical was gonna be similar." It's the latest setback in an injury-plagued career for Brooks, who has played just five of a possible 36 games since being drafted in 2024 due to two ACL tears — one at Texas and one as a rookie. With Brooks used sparingly through two games, Chuba Hubbard remains the clear starter, and Carolina is reportedly bringing in veteran Austin Ekeler to fill out the backfield behind him and A.J. Dillon. articles.title: From missing India's original  squad to making history with silver, Roshibina Devi becomes first Indian woman to win three successive Asian Games medals
articles.summary: Naorem Roshibina Devi's Asian Games journey began with uncertainty but ended with another medal.
articles.body: Naorem Roshibina Devi's Asian Games journey began with uncertainty but ended with another medal. The 25-year-old Manipuri wushu player won silver in the women's 60kg Sanda category after losing 0-2 to China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the final at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall on Thursday.With the silver, Roshibina became the first Indian woman to win three successive Asian Games medals in wushu, following her bronze at Jakarta 2018 and silver at Hangzhou 2023.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyFrom controversy to the podiumRoshibina was not part of India's original squad after losing the selection trial to Divyanshi Choudhary in June. Divyanshi was initially selected but was later withdrawn after the Wushu Association of India said an MRI showed a partial high-grade ACL tear.Divyanshi had alleged that she was being mentally and physically harassed and claimed Roshibina had been involved. The WAI rejected the allegations and said the squad change was made on medical grounds. The Sports Ministry subsequently approved Roshibina as the replacement.Roshibina, who learnt about her inclusion around September 10, said she wanted to move on from the controversy."What happened was not because of me. It was the federation's decision. Whatever decision the federation (Wushu Association of India) took, I think it was a good decision," she said."I will ignore it (the accusation). I just want to focus on my goal."Little time to prepareRoshibina had been out of the national camp for around one-and-a-half months after losing the trials and travelled directly from Manipur after being recalled."There was a lot of disturbance when I came here for the Asian Games. I did not get much time to prepare. If I had more time, I would have done better," she said.Her coach Amit Pal also pointed to the lack of preparation, saying Roshibina had only limited training after being named in the team on September 10.Despite that, she defeated Bangladesh's Shika Khatun in the pre-quarterfinals and Macao, China's Chu Man Sin 5-0 in the quarterfinals before securing another Asian Games medal.Roshibina could not match Zhang's aggression and technical superiority in the gold-medal bout. The Chinese fighter won both rounds unanimously, with all five judges awarding her 5-0 decisions.Zhang dominated the scoring in both rounds, particularly with her side-kicks."She (Chinese player) is a new player, I have not fought against her. She was good in her side kicks. I also tried to defend. I tried to throw her, but she did better," Roshibina said.The silver left her disappointed at missing gold."I have won silver earlier and this time also, I could win only silver. I could not give the gold medal to the Indian people. I could not give what everyone wanted," she said.Born in Kwasiphai Mayai Leikai in Manipur's Bishnupur district, Roshibina's journey has also involved considerable family sacrifice, with her farmer father Naorem Damu Singh selling a piece of land to fund her training and travel in the early years.Now, with three successive Asian Games medals, Roshibina has another target."I want to inspire all the players. I want to be like them. articles.title: 'Aur achha ho sakta tha': Mairaj Ahmad Khan after Indian skeet team's record medal haul at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian skeet shooter Mairaj Ahmad Khan believes India's historic run of three medals in skeet at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has created a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian skeet shooter Mairaj Ahmad Khan believes India's historic run of three medals in skeet at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has created a strong platform for the Los Angeles Olympics. Mairaj, who was part of the men's skeet team that won bronze, felt India could have done better and believed the team had a chance to win gold.India won medals in all three skeet team events over two days, with the men's team, women's team and mixed team all finishing on the podium.For Mairaj, the men's team bronze was his first Asian Games medal. He had previously competed at the Asian Games in 2006, 2010 and 2014 before returning to the continental event in 2026.Mairaj already has three World Cup gold medals - in New Delhi in 2021, Changwon in 2022 and Cairo in 2023. He also has a silver from Rio de Janeiro in 2016 and a bronze from Cairo in 2021.Apart from this, he has one gold, two silver and three bronze medals at the Asian Championships.Looking back at his individual performance at the Asian Games, Mairaj felt tiredness also played a role."In the individual event, hunger was not there. I think I was a little tired. I was relaxed, mentally tired, overworked. Maybe the calendar is so busy," Mairaj told TimesofIndia.com from Japan.Mairaj felt the team could have finished with gold but said there would be more opportunities to improve, with the World Championships and Asian Championships coming up."Aur achha ho sakta tha. We could have won gold medal. The stage was set but no propblem, next time," Mairaj said about the team's bronze medal finish.Proud of Anantjeet and ParinaazMairaj was particularly pleased with the performances of Anantjeet and Parinaaz in the mixed team event. He said he was proud of the way the two shooters performed and saw their medal as part of a bigger process.The men's skeet team of Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Mairaj and Bhavtegh Singh Gill won bronze on Wednesday. The trio finished with 346 points and then prevailed over Kazakhstan in a shoot-off to secure third place.Later that day, Raiza Dhillon, Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Maheshwari Chauhan also won bronze in the women's team event, giving India its first-ever Asian Games medal in women's skeet.On Thursday, Anantjeet and Parinaaz added another bronze in the mixed team event, giving Indian skeet medals in all three team events."I am really proud of the way Anant and Parinaaz have performed. We are building a team together for LA Olympics," he said.'I will not stop'Mairaj was clear that the Asian Games medals are not the end of the journey.He said his focus remains on improving and continuing the fight for the Los Angeles Olympics. The dream of winning gold, he said, has not changed."I will not stop. Ever since I picked up the gun, I have felt that I could have done better. I have made some mistakes," he said."The fight is on for the LA Olympics. articles.title: Pending 2027 NHL Free Agents That Could Get Traded During the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Given how life in the NHL goes, it's never too early to start thinking about trades. While all eyes are on Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, looking ahead to next summer's free-agent class shows us a lot of other players who could be moved this season.
articles.body:
Given how life in the NHL goes, it's never too early to start thinking about trades. While all eyes are on Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, looking ahead to next summer's free-agent class shows us a lot of other players who could be moved this season.

We haven't dug into the science, but players set to become free agents tend to be the ones most likely to be traded before the season is out. Whether their team feels it might not be able to keep them or another team wants to sell before the trade deadline, players at the end of a contract make the most sense to trade away.

Even though the list of potential free agents is really juicy right now, we know a healthy number of them won't make it to July 1 without an extension in place. That's why we're keeping our list a bit more realistic... in most cases, anyway.

Alex DeBrincat is a Michigan native who would like to stick around with the Red Wings. Unfortunately for him, whatever happens with Larkin may dictate how the Wings' season goes, and if it turns really bad, Detroit might be better suited to trade DeBrincat to cash in on a potentially juicy return.

DeBrincat was the Red Wings' leading scorer last season with 41 goals and 44 assists (85 points). He's been an electrifying goal scorer throughout his career in Chicago and Ottawa, and he's due for a big payday after this season is over as a free agent, whether he gets there or not.

No doubt that discussing an extension is on Detroit's to-do list, but they've been a bit, uh, messy this offseason, dealing with Larkin, searching for a new GM, and trying to re-sign RFA defenseman Simon Edvinsson. One thing at a time, apparently. If time gets away from them, trading DeBrincat is a real possibility. And you thought Detroit's year couldn't get worse!

All eyes will be on Minnesota this season, and not just because they're going to be a fun team to watch. They'll also be watching to see if/when Quinn Hughes gets traded for the second season in a row.

Wild GM Bill Guerin desperately wants to sign Hughes to an extension, and considering how brilliant he was from the moment he arrived in St. Paul, that's the right move. Then again, Quinn Hughes will cash in no matter where or when he signs, and with his two younger brothers already playing together with the New Jersey Devils, it's impossible not to think that's ultimately where he wants to go.

Whether that means a trade to the Devils or to another team ready to make Hughes the highest-paid player in the NHL the second he hops off the plane remains to be seen.

Then again, Guerin having all the time and ability to try to hammer something out gives him the advantage to either lock Hughes in for years to come or trade him before word gets out that he needs to do so to ensure a whopper of a return.

It's kind of wild to think that Erik Karlsson is in the final year of his contract and that he very well could be a great deadline pickup for a team one more time in his career.

The 36-year-old three-time Norris Trophy winner is coming off a fantastic resurgent season with the Pittsburgh Penguins after finding new life in coach Dan Muse's system. There's no reason to think he can't do that again this season and help spur Pittsburgh back into the playoffs.

But should things go sour for the Pens, and the playoffs get out of reach, Karlsson would be immensely attractive in the final year of his contract. Yes, he's got a whopper of a cap hit at $10 million, but that's lower than it should be because the San Jose Sharks ate part of it in the trade that sent him to Pittsburgh in 2023. A move at the deadline would make Karlsson's hit even more palatable, and his skills and abilities would ideally bring more than a few suitors.

Although our lists like this tend to focus on unrestricted free agents-to-be, it's hard not to look past some of the RFAs who are in awkward positions of their own with contracts coming up for renewal. None are more awkward than Columbus' Kirill Marchenko.

Marchenko had a thorny return to Blue Jackets training camp after he demanded a trade this summer. While he stated he loved hockey and enjoys being out there on the ice, when it came to doing all that in Columbus, he was a bit more evasive in his answers.

It's hard to imagine things staying cool with the Blue Jackets and Marchenko much longer, let alone for the rest of the season, and for a player of his skill and scoring ability, there's no doubt teams are interested in finding a way to add him.

Marchenko will no doubt command top dollar for an extension, and oddly enough, his RFA status has him in the driver's seat in a way, to pick where he wants to go. After all, what team is going to spend assets to acquire him if he won't sign long-term there either?

Much of how this season goes will determine what happens to a couple of the Boston Bruins' top free agents-to-be, and in Pavel Zacha's case, he could be in high demand if the Bruins fall out of contention.

Zacha has become a top two-way player in Boston and is coming off his most productive season as a pro. He had 30 goals and 35 assists (65 points), setting new career highs in goals and points. Since joining the Bruins, Zacha's offensive game has grown, and his defensive play has stayed steady from his years in New Jersey.

Zacha turns 30 in April, and while that age can be a bit scary for some GMs, others see it as a sign of the player being their ideal self. For teams in need of a top-six center with two-way ability, he'd make an ideal addition should things change with Boston in the standings or financially.

Some players have a way of finding their names in trade rumors all the time, and Ryan O'Reilly is one of them. Ever since he landed in Nashville, there's been idle chatter about him finding his way to another team, and now that he's in the last year of his contract with the Predators, that's not about to change.

What's working in O'Reilly's favor is that he's already won a Stanley Cup and a Conn Smythe Trophy with St. Louis in 2019, which makes him an ideal player for contenders to target in a trade. It also means O'Reilly won't just be cool with a trade to any team just for fun, either.

O'Reilly is 35 years old and still playing strong hockey. His defensive game is still solid; he's good on faceoffs and can still generate a ton of offense (74 points last season, including 25 goals). If Nashville is out of playoff contention, it's hard to imagine he'll still be there by the trade deadline.

Another young player who's set to be a restricted free agent this summer is Rangers defenseman Braden Schneider. What's interesting about him is that he was an RFA this summer and signed a one-year, $5.5 million contract. If it was a "show me" contract, it's a lot of money for one year to prove yourself, which means teams ought to be calling New York about his availability.

Schneider is 25 years old and has been a fixture on the Rangers' blue line for the past four seasons. He's a steady 15-to-20-point-a-year player, can move the puck well, and his advanced metrics are average-ish. You get the feeling the Rangers don't want to give up on a younger player but also lack internal options to push him, and efforts to change that from the outside have fallen short.

Schneider could be an ideal change-of-scenery candidate in a trade, but if fortunes change for the Rangers, he could benefit from that. Then again, 2026 first-round pick Alberts Smits might be the guy that causes a Schneider trade to happen if he takes the blue line by storm.

Things haven't looked positive for the Flames over the past couple of seasons, and as they head into a new year, they could be looking to tinker with the roster more, especially with forward Morgan Frost heading into free agency next summer.

Frost had his best season in three years last season, with 22 goals and 21 assists (43 points), and if he builds on that, it would help him land a raise on his $4.375 million cap hit this season. Since he became a full-time NHL player in 2022-2023 with the Flyers, he's been a steady 40-point-per-season player. The hope was that his offensive numbers would improve, and setting a career high with 22 goals last season might be an indicator that's happening now.

If Frost's offense continues to grow this season, the Flames will have a choice to make: offer him a raise on an extension or potentially trade him if he wants to test the market. At 27, he's unlikely to develop further as a player, but if his veteran savvy leads to more goals, he could be a sneaky addition for another team.

It's not to say that Casey Mittelstadt has been a perplexing player the past few seasons, but the offensive breakout we saw from him a few years ago with the Buffalo Sabres hasn't found its way to either Colorado or Boston in full. In Buffalo, he was nearly a 60-point player, but since then he's been around a 40-to-45-point player, still solid, but obviously not quite as potent.

Mittelstadt's skill is still very good. He possesses incredible hands, scoring instincts, and a quick offensive mind. As he enters the final year of his contract with the Bruins, whether his future lies in Boston or elsewhere, where his offense can shine more, remains to be seen. If the Bruins struggle this season, the chances of Mittelstadt being traded elsewhere would increase.

What's more interesting about his setup in Boston is that with J-J Peterka's arrival with the Bruins, Mittelstadt could end up on a line with fellow UFA-to-be Pavel Zacha, and that kind of arrangement could lead to both of them having career years with new contracts in the works. That would be a nice problem for the Bruins to have.

If it feels like we've been waiting a long time for Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin to get traded, imagine what it's been like for RFA-to-be Shane Wright. The Kraken made it clear they were looking to move the 2022 No. 4 overall pick.

Wright has been a change-of-scenery candidate for about a year now (at least it feels that way), and after seeing his point total go from 44 two years ago to 27 last season under new coach Lane Lambert, it's more than a cause for concern for everyone involved. He was an elite skill player in junior hockey and had a strong first pro season in the AHL at 19, but the situation in Seattle has been less than helpful for Wright.

What Seattle would want in a trade and what a team would offer almost certainly differ drastically, because Kraken management wouldn't want to have eggs on their faces if Wright breaks out somewhere else. Barring a breakout to start this season, Seattle moving him seems inevitable, if not overdue.

articles.title: Baltimore heads to Brazil with something to prove against Dallas
articles.summary: Baltimore will attempt to rebound from its fourth-quarter collapse against New Orleans when it faces Dallas in a much hyped matchup in Brazil
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will travel to Brazil carrying more than passports, equipment, and the expectations that come with one of the NFL's most publicized games of the season. They will also carry questions about how they respond to adversity.

Baltimore surrendered an eight-point fourth-quarter lead in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints . The Ravens will attempt to prevent that collapse from becoming a trend when they face the Dallas Cowboys at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

The Ravens led New Orleans 17-9 entering the fourth quarter but were outscored 15-0 over the final period. Baltimore produced only three second-half points, committed costly penalties and failed to capitalize on multiple possessions that reached Saints territory.

Lamar Jackson 's final pass was intercepted after the Ravens advanced to the New Orleans 37-yard line, ending their last opportunity to force overtime.

One loss does not define Baltimore's season. How the Ravens respond could reveal much more about their direction under Jesse Minter.

Baltimore handed Derrick Henry the football only 16 times against New Orleans despite playing with a lead for most of the afternoon. He finished with 68 yards and a touchdown as the Ravens ran just 22 times. Dallas enters Week 3 allowing 173.5 rushing yards per game. That creates an obvious opportunity for Baltimore to recommit to its most physical offensive player. A productive running game would keep the Ravens ahead of the chains while limiting possessions for Dak Prescott and Dallas' explosive offense.

The defense faces a more dangerous challenge.

The Cowboys responded to their season-opening loss by defeating Washington 37-20. Prescott completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns, while CeeDee Lamb produced eight receptions for 153 yards and two scores. Baltimore's secondary cannot afford the coverage breakdowns or extended drives that helped New Orleans complete its comeback. The Ravens must pressure Prescott without losing track of Lamb and Dallas' other playmakers.

The international stage adds to the spotlight.

Sunday's game will be the NFL's first regular-season contest in Rio de Janeiro. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at the historic Maracanã Stadium. The travel, unfamiliar surroundings, and heightened attention will test Baltimore's preparation. The Ravens cannot allow those circumstances to become distractions. Baltimore is 1-1, and there is no reason for panic. A disciplined performance against Dallas would turn Week 2 into a correctable setback. Another late collapse would create more difficult questions heading into October.

articles.title: Ravens’ stingy run defense meets a Cowboys ground game in trouble
articles.summary: Baltimore allows 83.5 rushing yards per game. Dallas averages 67.5, putting pressure on Dak Prescott in Brazil
articles.body:
Baltimore's run defense can shape Sunday's game in Brazil before Dak Prescott has a chance to get comfortable throwing the football.

The Ravens have allowed 167 rushing yards in two games, an average of 83.5 , while Dallas has gained just 135 , or 67.5 per game . The Cowboys are averaging 3.5 yards per carry and have produced only seven rushing first downs. Baltimore has permitted 3.6 yards per attempt, though opponents have scored three rushing touchdowns. The Ravens have contained yardage; they still have work to do near the goal line.

That distinction matters against Dallas. The Cowboys have shown they can score without a productive rushing attack. Prescott threw four touchdowns in their Week 2 win over Washington, distributing the ball to a receiving group led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Stopping the run alone will not stop that offense.

It could, however, narrow Dallas' options. Second-and-long and third-and-long would give Baltimore's pass rush more chances to attack Prescott. The Ravens have five sacks through two games, but the Cowboys have allowed only two. If Baltimore lets Dallas stay ahead of the chains, Prescott could continue working from a clean pocket.

The Ravens are looking to rebound from a loss in which New Orleans erased a fourth-quarter deficit. A strong run game would put Baltimore in favorable situations throughout the game. Finishing those possessions with stops, particularly in scoring territory, is the next step.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Breakout Star Tabbed As Final Hitter In Federal Gambling Investigation
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ outfield slugger is named in documents pertaining to a looming trial.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting a key piece of their lineup back at an important time of the season. Andy Pages returned from the injured list Tuesday to resume his role in the outfield as Los Angeles prepares for the postseason.

"Pages will make his return to the Dodgers after missing more than a month of action while recovering from surgery to address a left hand fracture," CBS Sports reported . "Once activated, Pages will likely take over as the Dodgers' everyday center fielder, pushing Tommy Edman back to second base and Alex Freeland into a bench role.

The timing of Pages' return comes at an important time for the Dodgers, who will be hoping he can recreate the World Series heroics that saw him make a stunning catch to overcome the Toronto Blue Jays last year. But it also comes alongside a more unexpected connection to one of Major League Baseball's biggest ongoing controversies.

Los Angeles Dodgers Slugger Andy Pages Plays Key Role In Pitch Rigging Case

Federal prosecutors have identified a pitch thrown to Pages in 2025 as the final one on a list of 18 throws at the center of their gambling case involving Cleveland Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase .

Prosecutors are focused on 18 pitches from 17 games ahead of the trial, according to the documents reviewed by ESPN's David Purdum . A pitch thrown to Andy Pages on May 28, 2025, in the ninth inning of a three-run loss to the Guardians in Cleveland is the most recent item on the list, according to Purdum.

Clase allegedly intended for the pitch to be a ball, but Pages swung at it and missed, turning the pitch into a strike.

Pages is not accused of participating in the alleged gambling scheme. Instead, prosecutors are expected to point to his at-bat against Clase in allegations that he and teammate Luis Ortiz had informed bettors of the velocity and results of their pitches in advance.

"The government will only seek to prove that for one or more of approximately 18 of Clase's pitches, and for two of Ortiz's pitches, the defendants provided advance inside information about their pitches to others, who bet on them," U.S. attorney Joseph Nocella wrote, per Purdum.

Los Angeles Dodgers, Andy Pages At-Bat Becomes Central To Looming Federal Trial

Alongside Pages, pitches thrown to several prominent MLB hitters are listed in the documents obtained by Purdum.

Jury selection for the trial is expected to begin in November.

"If convicted, each defendant faces a maximum sentence of 20 years' imprisonment on the wire fraud conspiracy count, 20 years' imprisonment on the honest services wire fraud conspiracy count, five years' imprisonment on the conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery count, and 20 years' imprisonment on the money laundering conspiracy count," the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York announced .

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane wants to be remembered for his character, not just his football
articles.summary: FC Bayern’s number 9 exudes class on and off the pitch
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the definition of a complete player: he can score, he can pass, he can assist, he can defend, he can cross and do so much more. Despite the qualities that he possesses, the England star wants to be remembered for other things on top of that.

"I want to be remembered as someone who puts the team above everything and who respects his teammates," Kane said in an interview with the Telegraph (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). "You're never bigger than your team, club or country. I've always worked hard, in silence and without showing off. Despite the highs and lows, I've always believed in myself and worked twice as much. I just want to keep doing it for as long as possible."

In a world where footballers would make everything about themselves, Kane never subscribed to that mindset. He has always made it a point to be a team player, to improve himself, and to simply enjoy the game as much as possible.

articles.title: Eagles Reunion Gives Zach Ertz One Final Shot at Incredible Franchise Record
articles.summary: Zach Ertz spent nearly five years stuck 10 catches behind Harold Carmichael in the Eagles' record book. He probably had a better chance of running into Carmi...
articles.body:
Zach Ertz spent nearly five years stuck 10 catches behind Harold Carmichael in the Eagles' record book. He probably had a better chance of running into Carmichael at the grocery store than catching another pass for Philadelphia .

Now Ertz is back with the team that traded him in 2021, and a record that seemed destined to stay out of reach is suddenly up for grabs. Philadelphia certainly didn't bring him back for a nostalgia tour. The Eagles are running out of healthy tight ends, and Ertz knows a thing or two about playing the position.

Eleven catches would put him atop the franchise's all-time receptions list. Getting them might be a little more complicated.

Eagles Reunion Gives Zach Ertz One Final Shot at Incredible Franchise Record

Carmichael finished his Eagles career with 589 receptions. Ertz had 579 when Philadelphia shipped him to the Arizona Cardinals in October 2021, ending a run that included three Pro Bowls and a Super Bowl championship.

He'd already caught the go-ahead touchdown against the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII. He'd also put together a ridiculous 116-catch season in 2018 , setting what was then an NFL record for tight ends.

Philadelphia handed the position to Goedert, and Ertz went about extending his career elsewhere. He spent time with Arizona and Washington before a torn ACL interrupted his latest chapter.

There wasn't much reason to think he'd ever get another opportunity to chase Carmichael. The Eagles had moved on, Ertz was getting older, and the record wasn't going anywhere.

Eagles Turn to a Familiar Face After Injuries Pile Up

Goedert's injury was bad enough. With Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers also unavailable, Philadelphia found itself digging through the available tight ends before September was even over.

The Eagles signed him to their practice squad Tuesday, although nobody should expect him to walk through the door and immediately start playing 60 snaps. He's 35, coming off major knee surgery and hasn't played a regular-season game since tearing his ACL with Washington.

That's quite a bit of rust to knock off.

Still, Philadelphia doesn't need Ertz to catch another 116 passes. A couple of third-down conversions, some help in the red zone and a veteran who knows where he's supposed to line up would be a welcome start.

The interesting part is what happens if Goedert misses several games.

Ertz wouldn't need a particularly heavy workload to catch 11 passes over a few weeks. Of course, that's assuming his knee holds up, he gets promoted to the active roster and Jalen Hurts actually looks his way.

A few assumptions for a guy who hasn't played in months.

Ertz Could Leave Philadelphia With One More Record

The Eagles host Chicago on Monday night, giving Ertz a few days to get reacquainted with an organization he once helped deliver its first Super Bowl championship.

His stay could be brief. Goedert will eventually return, and Philadelphia isn't going to keep its younger tight ends on the sidelines just so Ertz can chase a record.

But consider where he was a week ago. Ertz was unemployed, recovering from knee surgery and watching the Eagles play without him. Now he's back in Philadelphia with a legitimate opportunity to pass Carmichael.

And wouldn't it be something if a franchise record that survived more than four decades finally fell because Philadelphia couldn't keep its tight ends healthy?

articles.title: Hibs appoint Dutchman Reedijk as new manager
articles.summary: Former Beveren head coach Marink Reedijk vows to develop a "brave, intense and committed" Hibernian team after becoming the club's new manager.
articles.body:
Former Beveren head coach Marink Reedijk has vowed to develop a "brave, intense and committed" Hibernian team after becoming the club's new manager.

The Dutchman, 35, replaces David Gray, who was sacked eight days ago after a difficult start to the term for the Scottish Premiership outfit.

Reedijk has spent the last two seasons with Beveren, earning promotion to the top flight last season after an unbeaten campaign before leaving in the summer.

He previous worked in academy roles at Ajax and West Bromwich Albion, and in with the senior teams at KSV Roeselare, Vitesse and RSCA Futures.

Hibs say Reedijk - who is "honoured" to be appointed - arrives with a reputation for attacking football and building a strong team culture.

"I can feel the ambition and see the clarity of what the club is trying to achieve," he said. "That was a big part of what attracted me here.

"I want us to be an assertive team. A team that gives everything, plays with purpose and gives our supporters something to really get behind."

Reedijk will be assisted by Rogier Molhoek at Easter Road, with the club hailing his arrival as "an exciting moment".

The Edinburgh outfit are currently 10th in the Premiership, with two wins from their opening seven matches, and endured a gut-wrenching Conference League exit.

Under Gray, they finished third in 2024/25 and fifth last term, with the departed manager also leading them to November's League Cup semi-finals, where they will face city rivals Hearts.

Sporting director Malky Mackay insists Reedijk's recruitment is not about "changing the direction" of their footbal strategy, but is about "continuing to evolve it".

"We believe Marink is an excellent fit to take the team forward," he added.

"We began this process with a clear idea of the type of team we want to continue to build and the qualities we wanted from our next manager. Marink's philosophy, his work with players and his leadership style are strongly aligned with that.

"His teams are proactive, high energy and dynamic. What also stands out is his ability to develop individuals and create a strong collective environment."

Ross: Decent appointment, time will tell if it's the right one. His credentials and philosophy sits well with me and what we want to achieve. Welcome and all the best.

Lee: Another young manager! Let's get behind him, and the team and give him a chance to show what he is capable of. I hope it works out, because if it doesn't, beyond the dugout is where the spotlight should be.

Tony: Brilliant, good to have someone in quickly. Not a great knowledge of the guy but from what I've read he likes an attacking team with wingers so that's a positive. Will be good to see what he can do with the current squad. It probably won't solve it quickly but let's see.

articles.title: AEW’s Thekla on Unfiltered Promos, Growing Popularity & Going ‘All Out’
articles.summary: Plus, the 'Toxic Spider' also talks music, art and her surprising TV show binges.
articles.body:
Just as Spider-Man continues to rule the box office, one "Toxic Spider" looks to return to the top of the All Elite Wrestling food chain. Thekla's web of violence and carnage has made the Austrian a breakout star. She'll take on Willow Nightingale on September 26 at All Out for a shot at the Women's Championship, currently held by Mercedes Moné .

For Thekla, the pay-per-view event isn't just about being next in line at WrestleDream . The foul-mouthed member of the Triangle of Madness wants to defeat Nightingale after she dethroned her for the Women's Championship at Redemption in July.

Despite the performer's underhanded tactics and vulgarity that probably put the TBS and TNT censors on high alert, the rule-breaker continues to grow in popularity. The unpredictable livewire has connected with the audience in ways maybe she even didn't expect. Though in the world of pro wrestling precedence does exist with rebel "Stone Cold" Steve Austin a shining example.

Here Thekla sits down with a Capri Sun in hand to talk about her recent success and why what we've seen is only the beginning.

You're this despicable person on television, yet people have gravitated to you. What do you make of this?

Thekla: Yeah, I don't know what's wrong with people. Honestly, I always thought I was living on my own planet, with my own sense of humor and the things I like that not everybody else needs to like. Maybe people gravitate towards me being people who are just unapologetically themselves. I think that's something that everybody strives to be, themselves, but it's really hard. I guess that's kind of something that's entertaining to people, when they see somebody that is full-fledged whatever it is I'm f*cking doing, I don't know.

How much freedom do you typically have when it comes to what you say on the TV shows?

Apart from the usual stuff they try to make sure I don't say on TV? It's very hard for me not to say on TV that whole list of words that we get fined for. Other than that, I get to say pretty much what I want. I take a lot of inspiration from what I really like, and what I really feel, and what I think about people and myself. I get a lot more creativity than I thought I ever would. I get to choose more stuff than I probably should as well. So I get away with a lot of sh*t.

I have to ask. What's in those cups that you're drinking while cutting those promos?

That's a dumb b*tch question. Next question.

Okay, we'll keep that a mystery. But where do you find inspiration? I watch a lot of movies. I love a good movie and going to the cinema. I like books. I read a lot of autobiographies of people I find interesting. I'm a huge music person. I listen to a lot of music and the type of music then kind of inspires the way I feel. Right now, I'm in my Hispanic, Latin reggaeton phase, which might be surprising to some people. Then again, if you watch the way I'm having matches right now and dancing around the ring, maybe not. I'm just constantly listening to music in my head in general. My heroes are people like Iggy Pop, Lou Reed , you know, kind of like 60s, 70s, punk idols. I also love unapologetic characters. I like television. I'm also a big Quentin [Tarantino] fan. I'm watching a lot of old gangster movies from the 70s now. The type of Godfather type of stuff.

I am binging Curb Your Enthusiasm , watching the last stuff I haven't seen yet. I've been turned on to It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia a little bit. That's where the chaos comes from. I like a good chaos show.

How is it getting acclimated living in the United States and traveling throughout the country?

Well, what I don't love is the time zones. Americans, you got to get a hold of that because it's very confusing to people who are from here too. I love traveling. It's just cool. We did that Dynamite in the Midwest, and that part of America I haven't seen too much of yet. When we have two extra days in between Collision and Dynamite . Where we get to rent a car, drive around, and eat, and find a little shack on the side of the road. I love to go to a dive bar and stuff like that. I like the trashy Americana stuff too. Like broken blinking neon lights at night. Getting into wrestling, one of my number one things was that I wanted to travel and see the world, and I'm finally getting to do that. And I'm finally figuring out a way to not only go from airport to airport and hotel to hotel. Taking out big chunks and doing it right in a way where I can I feel like I'm getting to experience America, which is a f*ckin huge and cool and diverse country. It's insane.

Do you have a go-to travel partner or do you travel solo?

I mostly travel with The Dogs. We go way back because we were kind of a gang in Japan. Coming up in New Japan Pro-Wrestling and me with Stardom alongside Clark Connors, Gabe Kidd, David Finlay, those are the guys. It's also the smart bi*ches. You'll find me at the hotel bar with Lita Kross and Megan Bayne.

Speaking of Stardom, you're also the Artist of Stardom Champions with other Triangle of Madness members Julia Hart and Skye Blue. What has it been like seeing those two gain some fandom in Japan?

That has been huge for me. That is one of the main reasons I even went back to Japan after my one-year hiatus. It can be very hard when you don't have the backstory and the connections. For those girls, to make sh*t happen, because there's a language barrier and everything. It's really cool that we made it happen. That we got the titles. That Julia got to do the [5★STAR Grand Prix] is huge. I've still met so many legends. They're like, "I've never been to Japan. That's always been my dream. And Julia, especially, has been getting over so much. It's insane. We had another title match there two weeks ago. I know how they know me there, but just coming in and everybody just yelling, Julia, Julia. They're obsessed with her. I'm really happy. I'm really happy because I know I partly made that happen. I got, not only the connection to people who run sh*t, but also the story to make it make sense.

We're seeing returning faces like Britt Baker with other names potentially coming in like free agents Kairi Sane. What do you make of the landscape of the women's division right now in AEW?

I always like new faces coming in. I still consider myself a new face somehow. It has only been a little bit over a year for me. I'm a huge fan of people just going from one territory to the other, like in the old days. I'm very excited to see who's gonna step up, you know? Kairi has been the talk of the town. I'm only going to believe it once I see it. For the fans, it's always cool to see a new matchup. We'll see. Let's keep our fingers crossed. Let us see if we can pice it up a little bit.

This weekend you have your big match against Willow. You're building up this great rivalry. What has been like to work with her?

With Willow, we're seeing a different side of her. I've been known to bring out the worst in people, especially with a huge smiley babyface like Willow is. It's cool to see that f*ck you aggression come out. I don't like this b*tch, and I'm totally cool with that. That's the kind of energy I like. I think a little negativity, a little hate in the ring is good because it's about conflict. It's about not liking each other. I don't love a good handshake before a match. F*ck that. Let's make it messy. I think me and Willow, we might be a forever feud. That's the kind of stuff I like.

What does that potential match against Mercedes Moné mean to you?

it would obviously be a huge one. I've seen how people have been looking forward to it. A lot of people thought this was the match they were going to get to see at All In . When it happens, it's going to be big. It's going to be interesting. I know it is going to happen. When? Probably WrestleDream , maybe not, you know? Like, b*tches keep on getting hurt left and right. You never f*cking know. I'm hoping for the best, you know?

You have so many interests. Outside of wrestling, you also have been involved with music in groups like Death Row Groupies. Will we ever see you perform on the AEW shows, maybe as part of your entrance like Chris Jericho has done with Fozzy? Yeah, that's a hundred percent something I want to see. I have no idea where our drummer is. He might be dead in a ditch somewhere. You never know with my friends. I haven't heard from him in years. My other friend is somewhere stuck in Vienna. Who f*cking knows, I'm definitely going to go back to making music at some point. Whenever I get the opportunity, I think about doing an entrance with one of my past bands. Death Row Groupies isn't the only band I ever had. I'm also super interested in starting some new stuff. We got so many cool people who are capable of playing instruments. Maybe there's a Brody King-Thekla connection coming up sometime in the future. Who f*cking knows?

I'm also excited about seeing your work in the "House Show: Power, Spectacle, and Pro Wrestling" exhibit at the Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg next year. What can we expect?

I'm currently setting up my new studio here in Arizona. I'm planning on producing some new works, which people who know my art have been anticipating for a long time. I'm not sure yet what the medium is going to be. I'm probably going to start drawing a lot, and I'm still thinking about bringing out a new, um, art book after the last one ["K.O. City"] I did two years ago. So I've got a lot of unused material, and I've got some new ideas. That might be a surprise thing that I'm just gonna drop before the end of the year.

Have you ever got commissioned by Tony Khan or another one of the wrestlers to do a piece?

I have actually. Renee [Paquette] just recently asked me if I was open to doing commissions. I usually don't do commissions because my mind doesn't work like that. It's a lot. It's already f*cking hard to be creative, and then being creative under certain circumstances, is even worse. And I don't really care too much about the money aspect of it. Unless she gives me a really good idea, and it's like, "You know, that would be cool." And I say, "F*ck yeah, that's a great idea." Then I'd be willing to do whatever, we settle on. I might be doing a big piece for her [and Jon Moxley], actually, for their house.

You have a busy couple of months coming up. What do you want to see from your career and AEW beyond the obvious winning the championship again? See, that's hard for me because I came in so hot, and I've already done so many things. The only thing they took away from me was All In . And I'm kind of happy with that because otherwise I would have ticked all the boxes already. All the boxes, except for like coming up with cool ways to do an entrance and sh*t like that. I was holding the big one for seven months, I think? I already had really cool interactions with some of the best bi*ches we have on the roster. I remember they bring in stuff with people who are not wrestlers. Before I came to AEW, they did a feature with Doja Cat for one of her songs, and they had this little AEW music video. So I'd always be down to work with somebody who I mutually respect. That could be cool. As for wrestling, I got to do the strap match, which was the first women's strap match we had in AEW. That was sick. I could totally see myself doing a dog collar type of match. Those kinds of special rules, like first blood and that type of stuff. For that, I need a good feud. I don't like to get messy without a good story.

There is the potential of Blood & Guts again.

Exactly, exactly. Who knows? From how well it went last year, good or bad, I'm not sure. I still have some scars here. I just got a tetanus shot because we might be doing Blood & Guts again. You know, I'm not taking any chances, motherf*cker. I love my job. Let's put it that way. F*cking love my job.

articles.title: Presidents Cup Needs Fix After US Streak Dominates
articles.summary: The Presidents Cup struggles with predictability as the US dominates. Seven structural changes could save the event from becoming a mere corporate retreat.
articles.body:
The golf world gathers at the revamped Medinah this week, yet the air feels heavy with a lack of suspense. Fans are asked to pretend the event carries real competitive weight, but the reality is stark. The Americans hold ten of the top fifteen players in the world, a statistic highlighted by Data Golf. In contrast, the International Team boasts only one player in that elite tier, Si Woo Kim. This massive gap turns the biennial event into something resembling a corporate retreat rather than a true battle.

The United States has won ten consecutive Presidents Cups, holding a crushing 13-1-1 record over the years. The International Team's only outright victory dates back so far that many current competitors were not even alive when it happened. The event exists largely so the PGA Tour can maintain a store-brand version of the Ryder Cup, but the luster has faded fast.

While the tournament has produced memorable moments, like one of Tiger Woods' nastiest club twirls, these flashes do not fix the fundamental problem. Fans assume the US will win, and they are almost always right. No amount of marketing can change that mindset. MyGolfSpy argues that the format needs significant structural changes to create a closer competition and give the event a distinct identity.

The first major issue involves player eligibility. Because the PGA Tour operates the Presidents Cup, LIV golfers have been ineligible to compete. This rule has specifically prevented the International Team from selecting top talents like Joaquin Niemann and Cameron Smith. Without these players, the International side is severely weakened before the first ball is even struck.

The absence of these global stars creates a lopsided field that fails to engage the average viewer. The current roster selection process ignores the best players available, focusing instead on tour affiliation rather than pure skill.

Fixing this event requires bold moves that address the root causes of the imbalance. The most obvious solution is to let the best players compete, regardless of which tour they play on. This change would naturally solve many of the current issues before the next edition of the tournament takes place.

The International Team needs a realistic chance to win, and that chance disappears when top-tier talent is banned from the field. The current 13-1-1 record shows that the status quo is broken. A true competition requires both sides to have a legitimate shot at victory.

If the format remains unchanged, the event will continue to feel like a formality rather than a highlight of the golf calendar. The identity crisis must end, or the tournament risks becoming irrelevant to fans who crave genuine suspense and high-stakes drama.

Chelsea can't unilaterally recall Alejandro Garnacho in January, but that doesn't mean he won't be coming back in the winter market.

articles.body:
Frosinone sporting director Renzo Castagnini has revealed why Celtic's summer pursuit of Fares Ghedjemis ultimately failed despite the winger wanting to leave the Italian club.

Fares Ghedjemis of Algeria is seen in action during an international friendly match between Algeria and Guatemala at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on March 27, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

Celtic spent much of the transfer window attempting to bring the Algerian to Glasgow after initially missing out on his signature in January.

Martin O'Neill publicly admitted the Hoops had a "very strong" interest in Ghedjemis, but Frosinone stood firm despite approaches for one of their prized assets.

Ghedjemis had rejected the opportunity to join Celtic in January before helping Frosinone secure promotion to Serie A, but his position had changed by the summer and he was open to moving on.

However, a significant development behind the scenes at Frosinone altered the club's financial position and removed their need to cash in on the winger.

Speaking to Radio Sportiva, Castagnini said: "Ghedjemis wanted to leave, and I believe that when a player has the opportunity to improve, it's right that he shows it.

"When the Clara Vista fund came in, since we no longer needed to sell players, it was decided that Ghedjemis would stay with us.

"We're working on his new contract, so we're satisfied. We're doing things properly and calmly."

Frosinone president Maurizio Stirpe had previously insisted the offers received for Ghedjemis did not meet the club's valuation, with Celtic and Rangers eventually dropping out of the race as the Serie A side refused to budge.

articles.title: ‘Performative’ Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon ripped by ex-ESPN personality
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is facing criticism for her sideline antics during games.
articles.body:
If you're tuning into an Indianapolis Colts game, you never know what to expect to see on the field, but you know what you will see on the sideline: Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon .

Irsay-Gordon has become one of the most involved and present NFL owners since stepping into the owner role following the death of her father, Jim Irsay , in May 2025, and she has become a staple on the sideline during games.

On game days, you will see Irsay-Gordon patrolling the sideline with a headset so she can be in touch with communication between the staff, while holding a notepad to jot down her observations during the action. She also pops into team meetings.

Irsay-Gordon believes that learning the minor details of day-to-day operations helps her make informed decisions about how the franchise should move.

Oct 5, 2025; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon walks the sideline during the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Christine Tannous-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

"I think one of the things that I learned in going through, even as back as when we hired Chuck Pagano (in 2012), is that sort of accelerated my, ' I need to learn more about this, ' I need to be able to say, is this person full of BS? Do they even know what they're talking about?," she said in an interview with the team's website. "And I think one of the things that being on the headset has really helped me learn is to the question earlier, it's such a complex organism of football team and how it operates.

"You could say, 'Oh, that person ran that route wrong.' When you learn to find, 'Oh, someone tagged the wrong wide receiver, and it wasn't really the player's fault – it was the person that called it.' I think that's been very valuable, because it also helps us be able to know where do we need to make tweaks, what resources do we need, what do we need to fix. So much of it comes down to just how we operate and how things work and the headsets – I would suggest it for anyone else that has to pay coaches and GMs millions and millions of dollars. It helps you make a less expensive mistake potentially."

While Colts fans will love her dedication to the team, not everyone is on board. Former ESPN personality Ryen Russillo sounded off on the latest episode of The Ryen Russillo, calling Irsay-Gordon's actions "performative."

Ryen Russillo Calls Out 'Performative' Carlie Irsay-Gordon

"I want to see Carly Irsay's notes. I want to know what these notes are. It's very performative to me. I think her announcement is performative to the Colts fans that want her to be the hero for a team that is going through a disappointing run," Russillo said during his rant. "People could say that I'm only saying it because she's a woman, which would be total bullshit because Boston made fun of Robert Kraft forever because he brought a stopwatch to a workout.

"He walked around with a stopwatch and was manually timing people at workouts. When I see her do it, I want to know what, what are you writing down? Yeah. That's it. What are you writing down so that we have a better sense of what it is you're actually evaluating? Share the notes."

Russillo caught some immediate backlash in the comments section for his stance, with many praising Irsay-Gordon for her attention to detail and involvement in making sure the team is set up for the most success.

If the Colts can reach the playoffs for the first time since the 2020 season, it will be well worth the investment she has made in the day-to-day operations. And, at the end of the day, it's better to have an owner who cares rather than someone who is hands-off and just there to make money.

Carlie Irsay-Gordon, principal owner and CEO of the Indianapolis Colts, is photographed Thursday, Sept 25, 2025, in the trophy room at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis. Irsay-Gordon is holding a helmet worn by former Indianapolis Colts player Robert Mathis .

articles.title: Botín y Trittel se estrenan en el campo de regatas de la Copa América de Nápoles
articles.standfirst: Los españoles son el 50% del AC40 francés La Roche-Posay Racing Team. Este fin de semana se celebra la segunda preliminar en el mismo lugar que se disputará la 38ª edición
articles.summary: Los españoles son el 50% del AC40 francés La Roche-Posay Racing Team. Este fin de semana se celebra la segunda preliminar en el mismo lugar que se disputará la 38ª edición
articles.body: Diego Botín y Florian Trittel se instalaron en Nápoles, junto al resto de la tripulación del equipo francés La Roche-Posay Racing Team, a principios de septiembre. "Todavía nos estamos acostumbrando al tráfico, es una locura", confiesan. Volaron directamente desde el Gran Premio de España de SailGP, celebrado en Valencia, hasta la ciudad italiana en la que comenzará la 38ª Copa América dentro de ocho meses. No sólo tienen ya allí su base, también han recibido hoy mismo el AC75 con el que lucharán por ser el Desafío que trate de arrebatar la Jarra de las Cien Guineas al equipo neozelandés. Ha llegado esta mañana, procedente de Lorient, a Bagnoli, el barrio en el que se ha instalado La Roche-Posay Racing Team. Pero antes, este fin de semana, volverán a subirse al AC40, el barco con el que los equipos disputan las regatas preliminares. Esta vez en Nápoles, en el mismo campo de regatas en el que competirán en 2027 por el trofeo deportivo más antiguo del mundo. En la primera, celebrada en mayo en Cagliari, acabaron cuartos, por eso en la flota de la Copa América ya hay quien habla de La Roche-Posay como uno de los 'tapados'. "El objetivo es, sobre todo, poner en práctica lo que hemos progresado desde Cagliari y también lo que sentimos que todavía teníamos que dar allí. Fuimos uno de los barcos más rápidos en el recorrido, pero nos faltó consistencia en las salidas. Más allá de los resultados, la cosa se está poniendo cada vez más seria. Ya estamos aquí, donde vamos a tener la Copa América el año que viene, conociendo sobre todo el campo de regatas, que para nosotros es lo interesante", reconoce Florian Trittel, trimmer de La Roche-Posay y campeón olímpico, mundial y europeo de 49er junto a Diego Botín, que ejerce de patrón. Ambos son el 50% de la tripulación del barco francés. Quentin Delapierre, líder del proyecto, también estará al timón y Jason Saunders será el otro trimmer. Enzo Balanger y Timothé Lapauw completan la tripulación como reservas. Tanto Botín como Trittel sólo tienen buenas palabras para el campo de regatas. "Es excepcional para una Copa América. Tanto los vientos de componente más térmico, de sur y suroeste, como los vientos de tierra, de norte y nordeste, dan mucho juego. No es un campo monótono. Aunque sabemos que en la Copa América el barco prima mucho —los sistemas que tenga el equipo a bordo hacen que se navegue mucho mejor y pueden dar ventajas—, poder regatear bien también va a ser clave", aseguran. Los españoles llegan a la cita de Nápoles tras haber ganado el Gran Premio de Suiza de SailGP, también con catamaranes voladores, pero en ese caso F50. "SailGP y Copa América son dos eventos diferentes, en los que el estilo de competición es distinto. Sí que hay cosas que se pueden sacar del uno para el otro, pero son también equipos diferentes. Esta Copa América va a ser distinta de las anteriores porque los equipos saben bastante lo que tienen los demás. No va a haber grandes avances tecnológicos, pero vamos a intentar refinar nuestro barco y a ver si podemos dar ahí una sorpresilla", dice Botín. Los españoles están completamente integrados en el equipo francés y la unión es uno de sus puntos fuertes, como reconoció en la rueda de prensa previa Delapierre. "Todo se reduce a la confianza entre los cuatro tripulantes a bordo y creo que estamos en buena forma en ese aspecto. Esa es nuestra fortaleza, y este fin de semana daremos lo mejor de nosotros mismos", anticipó. A partir de mañana, se enfrentarán los seis equipos: Emirates Team New Zealand, GB1, Luna Rossa, Tudor Team Alinghi, La Roche-Posay Racing Team y se estrena el ARC Team USA. El desafío australiano todavía no. Se disputarán ocho regatas de flota. El viernes y sábado habrá tres regatas a partir de las 14:00 h. El domingo, dos más antes de sumar los puntos y que los dos barcos con la mayo puntuación pasen a la final. El Luna Rossa 1, que ganó la anterior regata preliminar, mantiene a Peter Burling como patrón y líder pero el resto de la tripulación será diferente con el copiloto Marco Gradoni y los trimmers Gianluigi Ugolini y Maria Giubilei. "Tenemos una alineación bastante diferente para el equipo y, además, en este último periodo nos hemos centrado mucho en el AC75, pero creemos que estamos en muy buena forma para rendir este fin de semana", reconoció el neozelandés, ganador de las tres últimas ediciones como patrón del Emirates Team New Zealand. Durante la rueda de prensa, Dylan Fletcher, el patrón del 'Challenger of Record' GB1, lucía una cicatriz en la cara tras una colisión con la lancha de seguimiento del Tudor Team Alinghi antes de la primera sesión de entrenamiento a principios de semana. No ha sido el único incidente de la semana. Harry Melges timoneará desde la cabina de estribor el ARC Team USA a pesar de haberse roto el pie al subir a una embarcación de apoyo neumática. "Fue un accidente fortuito, pero lo único que se necesita para navegar este barco es la cabeza y las manos, así que todo debería ir bien", dijo.
